package_info.package_versions: New variant (2020, as described in report)
package_info.why_malicious: Cerberus is a banking Trojan with enhanced Remote Access Trojan (RAT) capabilities, distributed via a compromised MDM server to employees' mobile devices. It exfiltrates sensitive data including credentials and SMS (including 2FA codes), representing a severe compromise of device and data security.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code requests permissions to read and receive SMS, access the internet, read contacts, and write to external storage, enabling the app to access sensitive data and exfiltrate it.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A banking app requesting broad permissions, especially SMS and internet, is a common pattern for credential theft and exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should only request permissions necessary for their function; requesting SMS and internet together is a red flag for malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate banking apps may request similar permissions for 2FA, but not in combination with RAT capabilities.
key_indicators: Request for SMS and internet access

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SmsManager smsManager = SmsManager.getDefault(); String sms = getSmsContent(); sendToC2(sms);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads incoming SMS messages (including 2FA codes) and sends their content to a command-and-control (C2) server over the network.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating SMS messages, especially 2FA codes, is a hallmark of banking Trojans.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps should not read and transmit SMS content to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some apps may read SMS for auto-filling OTPs, but should not transmit them externally.
key_indicators: Sending SMS content to remote server

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after installation, on device boot or app start)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if the accessibility service is enabled and, if so, uses it to escalate privileges, allowing the app to perform actions on behalf of the user and evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abuse of accessibility services is a common technique for privilege escalation and persistence in Android malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should not use accessibility services for privilege escalation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Accessibility services are used for assistive technologies, but not for privilege escalation.

attack_chain.action: MDM server is compromised and used to push the Cerberus APK to employee devices.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious app is installed on target devices.

attack_chain.action: Cerberus app requests broad permissions including SMS, internet, contacts, and accessibility service.
attack_chain.leads_to: App gains access to sensitive data and device controls.

attack_chain.action: Cerberus reads SMS messages (including 2FA codes) and exfiltrates them to C2 server.
Cerberus abuses accessibility service to escalate privileges and maintain persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: App can perform actions on behalf of the user and evade removal.

behavioral_signatures: Android app requesting SMS, internet, and accessibility service permissions together
Abuse of accessibility service for privilege escalation
file_indicators: APK distributed via MDM with unusual permissions
Presence of Cerberus-related package names or signatures
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Cerberus C2 domains/IPs
Unusual POST requests containing SMS or credential data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android apps installed via MDM that request SMS, internet, and accessibility permissions. Detect background services reading and transmitting SMS content. Flag apps abusing accessibility services for privilege escalation. Correlate outbound network traffic to known C2 infrastructure.
